newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel unveils satellite communications project.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel unveils satellite communications project.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom on Friday unveiled its "SkyBridge" global communications project that uses 64 low orbit satellites and said it planned to raise $3.5 billion in financing through debt and equity placements.
Alcatel's Alcatel Espace on Friday filed with the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) for an application to launch the project, which was formerly known under its code-name SATIVOD.
The project rivals such other satellite projects as the $9.0 billion system of Teledesic Corp, backed by Microsoft's Bill Gates and and cellular phone mogul Craig McCaw.
The SkyBridge system will be operational in 2001. Alcatel is looking for financial and industrial partners to share the project but aims to remain leading shareholder.
U.S. bank J.P. Morgan has been mandated to seek financial partners while talks with a U.S. industrial partner are far advanced, a spokeswoman said.
The SkyBridge system will provide high-speed, broadband, interactive services to business and residential users around the world.
In addition to Internet access, the system will provide bandwidth on demand for other types of high speed data communications at speeds up to 60 megabits per second.
